1.why: The typeface appears legible, but there is no clear indication of dyslexia-friendly spacing or font choice.

2.why: Instructions avoid italics and all-caps, but some text blocks (e.g., logs) are dense.

3.why: Content is readable and well laid out on mobile, with clear spacing and sizing.

4.why: Instructions are short and use plain language (e.g., 'Enter the 6 numbers when you are ready').

5.why: An example ('Example: 123456') is provided for the verification code input.

6.why: Most instructions are concise, but some screens (e.g., step_04) include longer error messages.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard option is visible for codes or secrets in any screenshot.

8.why: No QR code option is offered for code entry or authenticator setup.

9.why: No evidence of autofill or password manager support (e.g., no autofill attributes or icons).

10.why: Primary actions (e.g., 'Send code', 'Check code') stand out clearly with blue buttons.

11.why: Only one main action is requested per screen, though secondary actions (e.g., 'Send a new code') are present.

12.why: Feedback is provided (e.g., 'A code was sent'), but confirmation of next steps is inconsistent.

13.why: Users can retry (e.g., 'Send a new code') or re-enter codes without penalty.

14.why: Error messages (e.g., 'That code did not match. Check the 6 numbers or send a new code.') are specific and non-blaming.

15.why: No time limits are imposed on reading or entering codes; users can proceed at their own pace.
